doc.title: David Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2022

title: Trumpet maintenance routine and using pandemic time to improve
summary: Weiss describes trumpet practice as athletic maintenance (long tones, slurs) and how the pandemic let him and the Cookers go beyond maintenance, transcribing solos and practicing three or four hours.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Excuse me, what do you tend to practice?

It’s an interesting thing. This is what me and actually the other guys in Cookers were talking about at the beginning of the pandemic. When you’re playing a lot, ideally, with trumpet you’re basically trying to do maintenance. You know, like an athlete you know. You still, you know you still go to the gym, you still do weight training, whatever it is to keep you in the best shape you can be to do this thing. So that includes physical stuff and, I mean trumpet stuff is kind of calisthenicy. I mean you do a lot of long tones, do a lot of slurs, you do a lot of things just to kind of maintain whatever it is you’ve achieved at that point. And the thing about the pandemic was okay, you know we all had that like, oh wow, now well at least we’ll have this time to, you know, it’s not exactly a desert island or a cabin in the woods, but you have suddenly, like wow, this is going to be great. And I have all the time in the world to practice. But what we found after like — those guys

longer than me — but you know me for a considerable amount of time too, we found like oh wow, we can go past maintenance. You know we can actually start working on our craft again, like improving. And it took a minute to be like oh yeah, how did we do that you know. So I went back to basics. I started transcribing solos again, I started expanding the calisthenics and stuff that would probably either try and like improve my range or, you know, make me more consistent. So I was able to work out, you know, instead of like the one hour to keep your chops together, to two hours you know and kind of strengthen a little more, to three or four hours like you know let’s go for something that will actually make you, you know, exceed what you’ve done so far.
